liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cold Rain and Snow** (1 review): This source alone has the song from this night, undocumented elsewhere; audience-recording sound before and after matches, and the performance is good [6]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Pig Pen's stage rapping during Lovelight is a highlight worth hearing [12]
- **And We Bid You Goodnight** (1 other source): The show closes with And We Bid You Goodnight as the encore [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Deep Elementary Blues**: back after 206 archived shows (1205 days); rare: 12 archived performances [16]
- **Don't Ease Me In**: back after 218 archived shows (1343 days) [16]
- **Katie Mae**: rare: 10 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd70-03-20.sbd.yerys.1315.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 138 min; rated 2.17/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Hard to Handle is recorded much better than the first five tracks; the acoustic section falls between the two; The second electric section, starting with Good Lovin', sounds especially fine [8][9]
- **gd70-03-20.sbd.late.hamilton.14287.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 123 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound is generally good, but at times drops to low quality and becomes distracting; The second electric section, starting with Good Lovin', sounds especially fine; Hard to Handle is recorded much better than the first five tracks; the acoustic section falls between the two [5][10][11]
- **gd1970-03-20.sbd.smith.99182.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 106 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: This soundboard sounds excellent, free of the heavy tape hiss of the reviewer's old cassette copy; Sound is far cleaner than earlier copies: hiss is reduced and instruments are better separated; Soundboard mix puts vocals much louder than the instruments [3][12][13][15]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's mother attended this show and several other Capitol Theater concerts, and says the recording conveys the live atmosphere [5]
- The MC asks for a woman named Annete to come backstage to Pig afterward, inviting other pretty women too [7]
- A crowd member shouts an obscene peace-themed slogan during the show [7]
- The first five tracks match those of the 11 November 1970 Rock Palace show in Brooklyn, NY [8]
- The first five tracks match those of the 11 November 1970 Rock Palace show in Brooklyn, NY [11]
- The show has been overlooked, sitting after the strong February 1970 shows and before the better-known later spring shows [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-03-20.sbd.yerys.1315.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jared Minkoff and Ben Yerys; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Tracks are jumbled: the soundboard middle of the show comes first (tracks 1-9), then the show's beginning follows [6]
- **gd70-03-20.sbd.late.hamilton.14287.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Hollister, Brian Voelz, G.S. Hamilton; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [2]
- **gd1970-03-20.sbd.smith.99182.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Matt Smith; source: SBD > Reel [3]. Also: Source comes from the Will Boswell collection, transferred by Matt Smith [3]
